chapters.title: Recruitment & Selection Process Flow Chart
chapters.text:
## SELECTION OF PLACEMENT CONSULTANT
Recruitment Incharge along with Manager / Head HR empanel & select best placement consultant to source potential candidates. Selection of Placement consultant will be based on following factors:
- Technical & Functional Expertise
- Turn Around Time – Band / Grade Wise
- Resume Shortlisting Ratio
- Selection Ratio
- Cost of the Hire
- Candidate Tracking - Pre & Post Joining
- Poaching
## SCREENING OF CV’s
It is the prime responsibility of Recruitment Incharge to Screen Resume received from sources as stated above. Recruitment Incharge shall share resume along with Position wise Recruitment Tracker for Hiring Manager’s ready reference.
- Age verification of candidates before hiring.
- To prevent the child Labour, in advertisement of the recruitment we are mentioning the age limit clause which is 18 year and above.
- We are verifying the age before processing for interviewing candidates.
- Government identification proof provided by candidates such as Adharcard undergoes verification before the interview process.
## SHORTLISTING & PRIMARY INTERVIEW
Hiring manager shall revert to Recruitment Incharge with shortlisted resume & preferred timing & medium of interview. It is advisable to have Primary Interviews through Video Conferencing or Telephonic.
After interview Hiring manager needs to provide Interview assessment in the prescribed format provided by Recruitment Incharge. Based on assessment Recruitment Incharge shall coordinate with Interview Panel to schedule shortlisted candidates for further interview(s) as per availability of Interviewer & candidate.
It is advisable to shortlist more than two candidate for further round of interview.
Recruitment Incharge will source more resumes in case no one is selected from the given primary interview.
## PANEL INTERVIEW WITH HOD, HR HEAD & MD
- A panel interview will be lined up by Recruitment Incharge. It is advisable to have Face to face or Video Conferencing interview as it is the final step of selection. Recruitment Incharge shall provide Resume & primary Interview assessment sheet to the panelist for their ready reference.
Interview Panel shall use primary interview assessment sheet for recording their interview assessment. It is advisable to shortlist two candidate’s in view possible contingency if any.
## HIRING PROPOSAL
Based on assessment Recruitment Incharge in guidance with Manager / Head HR shall prepare Hiring proposal, which adhere Organizational Fitment & Compensation Proposal after collecting & examining following documents & then negotiating with the candidate.
- Candidate Latest Colour Photo & Photo Id
- Educations documents
- Professional documents
- Current employer appointment letter
- Last Three month’s Salary Slip
It is advisable to have Employee Background Verification for key / critical position before proceeding further. Recruitment Incharge shall identify & empanel such agencies.
Compensation & Benefits shall be offered as per OIL C&B structure & in view of criticality, urgency of the position. Hike up to 25% on candidate’s existing CTC can be given subject to adherence of the CTC brackets approved by Management. If needed negotiation has to be done with candidate keeping in mind, salaries of comparable existing employees, salary band for the level of the candidate, current salary of the candidate and candidate’s expectations.
Any deviation in the same has to be discussed & approved by the Management.
It is Recruitment Incharge responsibility to explain OIL offer to candidate & clarify all doubts. There should be no scope for communication gap / ambiguity.
## TRAVELING EXPENSES FOR OUTSTATION CANDIDATE
Outstation candidate (not staying in Maval & Haveli Tahasil OR candidate having > 120km total distance from the interview location) called for personal interview will get reimbursement of traveling expenses as below.

chapters.title: Joining & Induction Process – Staff
chapters.text:
Induction focuses on Pre Joining & Joining formalities. It is mainly about connecting new employee with the bureaucratic, hierarchical and technological systems used across the company, so that new employee can start plugging to these systems.
## Pre Joining - 1 Day Prior to Joining
- RI shall send a Welcome Mail to new employee & have a call with his to brief him about commuting, joining documents etc.
- It is advisable to take acknowledgement of Welcome Mail from the Candidate.
- RI must inform Name of the new employee to Security personnel.
- RI ensure readiness of workplace & other infrastructure as well as Joining Kit & Induction schedule.
## NDUCTION - Joining Formalities – Day -1
- RI must meet & welcome new employee & make him / her confirmable.
- Offer Tea, Breakfast to new employee
- RI must collect, examine all personal, educational & professional documents with Original. In case of any deficiency RI must take advice of Manager / Head HR before proceeding for Joining.
- RI must ensure that all necessary forms are filled & signed properly.
- Carry out biometric attendance & allocate employee code as per the standard system.
- RI must provide Welcome Kit, Policy manual & Code of Conduct (Hard Copy) with New employee for his / her information & future reference.
- Meanwhile RI must publish Welcome Note as per the standard format.
- After completion of joining formalities RI must allocate resources to the new joining.
- It is advisable to identify & nominate a Mentor with the help of HoD & Head HR, who can build confidence & make upright impression about the organization.
- RI shall coordinate with WCM department for inducting WCM Compass room.
- WCM study material shall be provided to New Joiner for self-study & future reference.
## Collaborating with Organisation – Day 2
- RI must provide Induction schedule with Safety, WCM & other relevant functions & ensure it is been followed strictly.
- RI must release appointment letter & System access to new employee.
## ONBOARDING PROCESS
Onboarding process will focus on understanding, accommodating & establishing business relation.
It is a long term process where employee, HoD & organization try to get best out of the available skills & opportunities.
## Employee Feedback
7 days Feedback: RI shall take feedback from new employee after 7 days which will help Organisation to identify the problems faced by new employee & the area of improvement. RI must work out to close all the concern raised within next 8 days.
30 days Feedback: RI shall take feedback from new employee after 30 days which will help Organisation to identify pain areas of the position & the new employee. RI must put it to HoD & Head HR to resolve it within 15-20 days.
## Goal Setting
It is important to bring employee in to the system & have objective performance measurement system, which help employee & organization to monitor performance level. HoD must identify & communicate new employee regarding his KRA on which performance will be assess. It is RI responsibility to get it done.
## Performance Assessment
RI must process for the new employees’ performance assessment & HoD feedback on it. Based on it HR & HoD needs to discuss with the employee to decide his future assignments.
## NDUCTION & ONBOARDING – BLUE COLLAR
Blue-collar employee Induction focuses on
Joining & Induction formalities.
It is mainly about making new joiner familiar
with the systems, process & practice.
## NDUCTION
- Administration Dept. shall collect & verify relevant documents of the new joinee & ensure that needed documentation is done as per required.
- Administration Dept. shall carryout his biometric registration & induct him in LMS system.
- Administration Dept. shall issue Uniform, Safety Shoe & ID card etc.
- Mandatory training for ALL new operators
- Admin (Time Office)
- Safety
- WCM – Advise to Visit to Compass Room
- Function Specific trainings for ALL New Production operators
- Process Engineering
- Quality Assurance

chapters.title: Remuneration Policy
chapters.text:
## Job Classification and Pay Rates
- Job Classification: Positions in the company will be classified using a structured job evaluation system, taking into account factors such as skill level, experience prerequisites, job intricacy, and physical demands.
- Compensation Structure: Each job classification will be associated with a designated base pay rate, fostering internal equity and conformity with industry benchmarks. Market research and salary surveys may be utilized to ascertain competitive pay rates.
## Compensation Components
The remuneration package consists of the following elements:
- Base Salary: A fixed regular pay rate corresponding to the assigned job classification.
- Shift Differentials: Supplementary pay premiums for working specific shifts, such as nights or weekends.
- Performance-Based Pay: Implementation of incentive programs to reward surpassing performance targets, such as productivity bonuses or safety incentives.
- Overtime Pay: Compensation for employees exceeding their scheduled hours at an overtime rate, as dictated by relevant laws and regulations.
- Benefits: Provision of a comprehensive benefits package, encompassing health insurance, paid time off (PTO), and retirement plans (specifics detailed in a separate
benefits manual).

| Performance-Based Pay | Implementation of incentive programs to reward surpassing performance targets. | Productivity bonuses up to 10% of base pay; safety incentives include annual bon |
| Overtime Pay | Compensation for employees exceeding their scheduled hours at an overtime rate. | 1.5 times the regular hourly rate for hours worked beyond the standard 40-hour w |
| Benefits | Provision of a comprehensive benefits package, encompassing health insurance, pa | Health insurance covers 80% of medical expenses, 20 days PTO annually, 5% employ |
## Review and Adjustments
- Periodic Evaluation: Base pay rates and other compensation elements will be reviewed regularly, such as through annual assessments. These reviews will ensure our compensation remains competitive with market trends, accommodates cost of living adjustments, and adheres to internal equity standards.
- Performance Assessment: Employee contributions will be evaluated through structured performance assessments. These evaluations will guide decisions regarding merit-based salary adjustments and opportunities for career advancement.
## Communication
- Transparency: All compensation and benefits information will be communicated clearly to employees through accessible channels such as the company intranet, employee handbook, and during the onboarding process.
## mplemented Communication Channels
- We maintain up-to-date compensation and benefits information on the company intranet, including detailed breakdowns of salary structures, overtime policies, shift differentials, and comprehensive explanations of all benefits.
- Our employee handbook features a dedicated section on compensation and benefits, offering clear examples and scenarios to enhance understanding. Each component is thoroughly explained to ensure transparency and clarity.
## Communication of Compensation and Benefits
- Onboarding Process: During onboarding, HR presents new hires with a detailed overview of their compensation package. This includes interactive Q&A sessions to ensure understanding and address any initial questions.
- Annual Reviews: We conduct yearly reviews of all compensation and benefits information to maintain accuracy and relevance. Adjustments are made to reflect policy changes or legal updates.
- Real-Time Updates: Any immediate changes to compensation structures or benefits due to policy updates or legal requirements are communicated through the company intranet and via direct email alerts.
- Clear Communication: Compensation and benefits details are available through the company intranet, the employee handbook, and as part of the onboarding process.
- Open Dialogue: Employees are encouraged to discuss any compensation concerns with their supervisors or the HR department.
## Legal Compliance
- All compensation practices will strictly comply with applicable federal, state, and local wage and hour laws, including minimum wage requirements, overtime regulations, and the principle of equal pay for equal work.

chapters.title: Equal Opportunity Policy
chapters.text:
## Purpose
At Ognibene India Pvt Ltd, "Respect for Diversity" is one of our core values, and we are dedicated to being an equal opportunity employer. This commitment is reinforced by our Corporate Business Principles and Code of Business Conduct.
"Our success is driven by our people. We treat everyone with respect and dignity and promote a culture of personal responsibility. We recruit capable, motivated individuals who respect our values, provide equal opportunities for their growth and advancement, safeguard their privacy, and do not tolerate any form of harassment or discrimination."
"We embrace diversity and uphold the personal dignity of every employee. Ognibene India Pvt Ltd is committed to maintaining a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. As such, employees are expected to avoid discrimination based on origin, nationality, religion, race, gender, age, or sexual orientation, and to refrain from any verbal or physical harassment on these or any other grounds. Employees who feel their workplace does not adhere to these principles are encouraged to bring their concerns to the HR Department."
At Ognibene India Pvt Ltd, we ensure that all professional development and promotion processes are conducted in a fair, non-discriminatory manner.
## Scope
The Equal Opportunity Policy applies to all job applicants and employees at Ognibene India Pvt Ltd.
## Policy Framework
- Ognibene India Pvt Ltd is committed to providing equal opportunities without discrimination based on age, color, disability, origin, nationality, religion, race, gender, or sexual orientation. We do not tolerate any form of verbal or physical harassment related to these or any other grounds. To this end:
- Our employees are personally responsible for treating one another with respect and dignity, which includes acknowledging and honouring the rights and differences of others.
- Employment decisions at Ognibene India Pvt Ltd will be based on merit and not on any irrelevant attributes or characteristics an individual may possess.
- Developmental and promotional opportunities will be awarded based on performance, ability, and potential, in alignment with the needs of the business.
Ognibene India Pvt Ltd will not tolerate harassment, discriminatory behaviour, or actions that victimize any individual or group in our workplace. Appropriate actions will be taken based on investigations if employees breach this policy through discrimination, harassment, bullying, or victimizing others, or by making false claims.
If an employee feels they are being subjected to discrimination, harassment, bullying, or victimization, they can raise the issue with the HR department or utilize existing grievance redress mechanisms, such as the Speak Up program or contacting the ombudsman confidentially via telephone, email, or letter. All grievances and complaints will be taken seriously and handled with sensitivity and fairness.
In compliance with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016 and related rules, Ognibene India Pvt Ltd will ensure that appropriate infrastructure and reasonable accommodations are provided to enable persons with disabilities to effectively perform their duties. We have established a designated Diversity & Inclusion Council to oversee the provision of necessary infrastructure and facilities for the recruitment process of persons with disabilities. Ognibene India Pvt Ltd is committed to ensuring that no opportunities are denied to individuals from minority groups, and there will be no discrimination in any form.
## Roles and Responsibilities
## Employee Responsibilities
## All employees of Ognibene India Pvt Ltd have the following responsibilities:
To comply with this policy and all applicable laws and regulations. Compliance is mandatory whenever an employee is acting in their capacity as a representative of the Company.
## Responsibilities of Managers and Supervisors
## Managers and supervisors have the following additional responsibilities:
To take reasonable steps to resolve complaints that are brought to their attention and to maintain confidentiality to the greatest extent possible.
## Human Resources Responsibilities
## Human Resources representatives have the following additional responsibilities:
To provide guidance and address grievances related to the employment of persons with disabilities, as well as any complaints regarding discrimination in any form against any job applicant or employee.

- It is essential that all employees avoid or disclose commitments and relationships that involve, or could involve, a conflict of interest with OIL. A conflict of interest can exist if you have direct or indirect personal interest in a decision where that decision should be made objectively, free from bias and in the best interests of OIL. It is important that even the appearance of a conflict of interest be avoided.

Anything that could present a conflict of interest to an employee could also present a conflict of interest if it is passed on to a family member or a third party who is receiving benefits for the employee. chapters.title: Confidential Information, Intellectual Property and Data Protection
chapters.text:
This includes technical information about products or processes; vendor lists or purchase prices; cost, pricing, marketing or service strategies; non-public financial reports; customers’ lists; and information related to diversifications, mergers and acquisitions.
Intellectual property (IP) includes: know-how, patents, copyrights, trademarks and trade secrets.
Confidential information, including that which relates to IP, is a valuable asset that could benefit a competitor if known to it or otherwise harm the Company if made public. We must be careful not to disclose such information to unauthorized persons, either within or outside Ognibene and must exercise care to protect the confidentiality of such information received from another party.
Confidential information can be protected under the law as a trade secret if it has value to others and the owner takes the necessary steps to protect it.
Employees must not disclose or use any Ognibene confidential information for personal profit or advantage during or after their employment with Ognibene.
Employees who are entitled to discuss confidential information must obtain a written confidentiality undertaking (Non-Disclosure Agreement- NDA) from persons outside the Company (Including Consultants) before making any disclosure of confidential information.
Employees must obtain competitive information only in accordance with sound business and ethical principles and when approached with any offer of confidential information, must ensure that both parties understand and accept the conditions under which the information is received; and
We must always protect Company’s confidential information IP rights and we must also respect the same rights of others.
Company’s trademarks, brands and trade names are among our most valuable assets. The presentation, use and protection of Ognibene trademarks, brands and trade names are governed by the corporate identity.
We must not copy software protected by copyright law or license agreements, unless the owner of the copyright or licence holder specifically grants permission to do so.
Data may only be collected, stored, used and transmitted within the group or to third parties pursuant to Data Protection Laws applicable in various countries.
Any concerns in this will be addressed by IT & Human Resources Department.
- Drugs/ Alcohol/ Gutkha, Tobacco Chewing or Smoking etc.
It is forbidden to possess or consume illegal drugs while working in OIL premises or while working in the premises of Customers or Suppliers of OIL.

Company Property is for Company Use. Any suspected fraud or theft by employees or third parties must be reported & liable for legal proceedings.
There are some activities may have benefits to OIL as well as to an individual employee and the distinction between the two may be difficult to establish. Accordingly, it is important that any use of OIL property or services that is not solely for the benefit of OIL be approved in advance by your Departmental Head.

In the conduct of our business, government relations include all contacts with governments, their agencies and representatives, in local, national & international jurisdictions around the world.
Only nominated employee will interact with various government agencies in accordance with established practices and procedures based on the need of his / her roles & responsibility. Same is applicable for the non-government agencies such as Labs, Auditing Firms etc.
## Offering and Granting Advantages
We sincerely take lot of efforts to receive orders with the quality and the price for our manufacturing products and services.
No employee may directly or indirectly offer or grant unjustified advantages to others. Including employees of OIL in connection with business dealings neither in monetary form nor as some other advantage even at the cost of forgoing business opportunities.
Gifts to business partners’ employees must be selected in appropriate manner to avoid any appearance of bad faith or distortion of judgment in the mind of the recipient. Employees concluding contracts with consultants, agents, or other intermediaries must see that they do not offer or grant unjustified advantages.

No employee may use his or her position to demand, accept, obtain, or be promised advantages. This does not apply to the acceptance of occasional gifts of insignificant value, but any other gifts must be refused or returned.

chapters.text:
## STAFF INDUCTION TRAINING
## ntroduction
OIL is committed to inducting all new employees into the organisation, in order to ensure that they have a smooth integration into their role and become operationally competent.
Induction programs, which are well planned, conducted and evaluated, will enable new employees to learn about the organisation, its culture and the requirements of their role.
## Purpose
The purpose of this document is to ensure that new employees have a smooth transition into the organisation and their roles.
## Definitions
New employees refers to both recruits to the company (including permanent staff, casuals and temporary staff), and staff transfers.
## Policy
This Policy applies to employees responsible for conducting Inductions within OIL.
## NDUCTION TRAINING PROCEDURE
## Responsibilities
It is the responsibility of the HR Head to ensure that:
- Recruitment Executive is assigned who will be responsible for arranging the induction of new employees;
- All new employees participate in an induction program.
It is the responsibility of the Recruitment Executive to ensure that:
- An induction kit is developed; containing relevant documents like brief about company, org chart, contact details safety Norms etc.
- The induction kit is kept up to date with relevant information;
- The quality of the induction process is maintained.
It is the responsibility of the Human Resources Department to ensure that all employees of OIL are notified of any new starters by way of welcome note.
## Procedures
The T & D /Recruitment Executive to schedule all new employees to attend an induction on their first day of employment, nominating the area where the induction will be conducted and ensuring all necessary resources are available (e.g. enough chairs, overhead projector, refreshments, etc.). Or with individual HOD as per time slots available .
An appropriate amount of time and expenditure should be used to ensure the communication of required information, such as Occupational Health & Safety requirements, duties to be undertaken, dealing with clients/customers, physical layout of the site, WCM procedures etc. This will ensure that employees can work safely and represent the organisation effectively.
The T & D/Recruitment Executive should tailor the induction program to suit the needs of the employee(s) being inducted and provide the appropriate information to the new employee(s).
The T & D/Recruitment Executive is responsible for following up the employee’s induction during the first week and month as indicated on the Induction Schedule (see Appendix A).
The T & D/Recruitment Executive should work through an Induction Schedule for each new employee, ticking each item as it is addressed and crossing out those items not applicable. They should ensure that the new employee and the appropriate Manager sign the Induction Schedule on completion.
## Follow Up
The T & D/Recruitment Executive should ensure that each employee completes an Induction within the stipulated timing as mentioned in the Induction Schedule.

chapters.title: Performance Management System
chapters.text:
## PURPOSE:
- To define and maintain guidelines for effective, consistent, fair and cordial Performance Management System.
## OBJECTIVE:
- Define Methodology of Performance Management System (PMS).
- Define PMS & Appraisal Cycle
- Define Performance Measurement Parameters / Quantifiers
- Monitor & Communicate Performance Feedback.
- Define Employee Development Plan
## APPLICABILITY :
- This policy will be applicable to OIL on roll staff employees.
## RESPONSIBILITIES:
- HR department is responsible for preparation, & execution of the policy.
- HoD are responsible for adherence of the policy.
## METHODOLOGY OF PMS – BALANCE SCORE CARD
- OIL has accepted Balance Score Card, which is a strategic performance measurement model to manage the implement Strategy, measures the performance beyond mere financial & communicate the vision strategy & performance expectation to the team.
- Objective of this is to translate an organization’s mission and vision into actual actions. The actions are set up with measurable indicators that provide support for understanding and adjusting the chosen strategy.
- The starting points of the balanced scorecard are the vision and the strategy that are viewed from four perspectives: the financial perspective, the customer perspective, the internal business processes and learning & growth.
## Define PMS & Performance Cycle
- Following is the modest explanation of PMS & Performance Cycle

## ANNUAL PERFORMANCE REVIEW
- Every employee performance will be judge on the basis on achievement of KRA. Employee has to maintain & present KRA tracker on which final KRA assessment can be done.
## Merit Increase
- As a part of continuous improvement to strengthen performance review process, we use BELL CURVE method of performance rating.
- It is always important to identify top-performers and reward them substantially. This helps the organization to retain the top talent with them. This way both the employee and the organization grow.
- Bell curve is probably the only method by which managers in the organization can implement leniency or strictness of ratings. If the managers implement leniency in their rating a large majority of employees will fall in the high rating group. If the managers implement strictness in their rating, a large majority of the employees will fall in the low rating group, which will demotivate the employees. So on average, most managers tend to rate on a lenient scale.
- This evaluation system helps identify the suitability of employees in a job position. By doing forced ranking with adequate analysis and HR interventions we can identify the strengths and areas of improvement of the employees and place them in positions, which map better to their capabilities and balances the appraisal mechanism of all managers.
## MERIT INCREASE TIME LINE
- To have on time Performance Review & Merit increase, HoD are required to start & finish the process in the month of March only. Following time line will help to understand the process in more better way.
## Promoting Career Mobility:
- On the basis on evaluation of ability & performance, potential we promote internal career mobility within the organization through prior essential training and guidance.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.text:
## Working Days:
- OIL will be working for 6 days per week i.e. Monday to Saturday & 52 weeks per year.
- Refer Leave Policy for Annual Working day, Leave Days, Paid Holidays etc.
## Weekly off:
- Every employee will be having one day week off per week.
- Support functions like Core Team, Finance, Purchase, IT, HR etc. will have Second Saturday off in addition to the all Sunday off.
- Management can make changes as per the business need or other reasons such as Electricity Shut down day etc.
## Shift Working
- Every employee has to follow shift schedule displayed by Head of the department.
- Employee can change shift with the approval of HOD. Employee must fill Shift Change application & get approval by HoD one day prior to shift change day.
- Shift change request can be considered for maximum two time in a month with an adjustment of reliever.
## Late Coming
- Employees shall not be permissible for late attendance in first Half. Attendance and punctuality are strictly monitored. Employees are advised to meticulously follow the shift timings
- Although late coming is not encouraged, yet in exceptional cases, cumulative late arrival up to 30 minutes on three occasions in a month, may be permitted which will be at discretion of management.
- Employee will have to take special sanction from the Dept. Head to regularize the late coming.
- Late coming of more than three times in a month will be treated as Half day attendance and will be liable for salary / leave deduction accordingly.
- Core team members will have flexibility for late arrival or early going for not more than 1.5 hours of start of shift with limited maximum for 4 times in a month and same must be pre-approved by MD.
## Working on Week Off / Paid Holiday
- Considering business requirement, employee may be called upon to work on Weekly Off / Paid Holiday.
- Employee should make himself available & ready for such calls.
- Avoiding such calls/responsibilities shall be considered indiscipline and appropriate action will be taken against him/ her.
An employee at all times, diligently and faithfully shall serve the company and devote his whole time and attention exclusively to the business and interest of the company and with the best of his skills shall carry out his duty and shall attend punctually at the place or places where he is, from time to time, employed.

chapters.title: Flexible working hours Policy
chapters.text:
- Flexible working hours are available to all full-time employees who have completed
their probationary period and have demonstrated reliability and accountability in their
roles.
- While flexibility is encouraged, all employees are expected to be present during core
- hours from 09:00 AM to 5:30 PM, ensuring adequate coverage and collaboration
- within teams.
- Employees may choose from various flexible working arrangements, including compressed workweeks, flexitime, or staggered shifts, subject to approval by their supervisor and departmental needs.
- Telecommuting options are available for eligible employees, enabling them to work remotely for a portion of their scheduled hours, subject to approval and adherence to company policies and guidelines.
## Over Time
- Employee up to Executive / Engineer position will be eligible for Overtime Payment except maintenance department where overtime payment will be eligible below Assistant Manager.
- Employee will get overtime for
- Working more than 02 hours beyond normal workings hours
- Working on Weekly Off
- Working on Paid Holidays.
- It is employee’s responsibility to get approval of their Overtime hours within Two days.
- However, HoD must be ensured that no employees are working in Company for continuous of two shifts.
- Delayed approval will not be considering for salary processing.
- Overtime hour will be paid at double the rate of average monthly wages for the hours of overtime work done during the month, along with the salary for the following month.
- The employee shall not be eligible for compensatory off or overtime pay for travelling after office hours and on weekly off, Sunday or any other paid holiday.
## Out Duty
- Employees may need ro go out of office for official purpose, in this case employee has to fill Gate Pass, get it approved by HoD & HR Department.
- Employee has to submit duly filled & signed Gate Pass to Security department at Main gate before leaving the premises
- Employee must register his or her out attendance in attendance system.
## Gate Pass
- Employee has to fill Gate Pass if he is leaving office for whatsoever reason, before end of his shift.
- Said Gate Pass duly filled & approved by respective HoD & HR Department otherwise security will not allow employee to go outside the company premises.
- No adherence of this will be consider as misconduct & disciplinary action will be initiated.

chapters.title: Gratuity
chapters.text:
- All On roll & contract employee, based on the eligibility criteria set by government bodies on regular interval will be covered under Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 which is a lump sum amount paid as a sign of gratitude for the services provided.
- An employee needs to have at least five full years of service at Ognibene India Private Limited , except in the event that an employee passes away or is rendered disabled due to accident or illness, in which case gratuity must be paid.
- Gratuity is paid when an employee:
[table]
| Retirement | Termination |
| Voluntary Retirement Scheme | Disabled due to accident or illness |
| Resigns after 5 yrs of continuous service | Death of an Employee (to the nominee). |
- Calculation of Gratuity will be as per the government guideline which is as below
- Gratuity = Last Drawn Basic & DA × 15 / 26 × No. of Years of Service
- Normally gratuity payment will be release within 30 days from date of separation of employee.
- All rules which are not covered in aforesaid points will be applicable as per.
- As per the gratuity rules, employers can forfeit to pay a gratuity of the employee who has been terminated for the following reasons –
- Committing an offence involving moral turpitude. (नैतिक अपराध को शामिल करते हुए अपराध करना)
- Riotous or disorderly conduct or any other violent act.(दंगा या कोई अन्य हिंसक कृत्य)
- OIL will adhere all the provisions, rules & regulations, procedures regarding contribution, payment or whatsoever as per the payment of Gratuity Act 1972 & government guidelines.
- Payment of gratuity may attract taxes as per the government guidelines.
## Payment of Bonus / Exgrtia
- As per the recent amendment, if an employee’s Basic + DA is less than 21,000/- then employer must pay Bonus at the rate of 8.33% of Basic + DA.
- If an employee’s Basic + DA is higher than 21,000/- then OIL will pay exgratia at the rate of 8.33% of Basic + DA subject to available & allocable surplus.
- OIL will adhere all the provisions, rules & regulations, procedures regarding contribution, payment or whatsoever as per the payment of Gratuity Act 1972 & government guidelines.
## Maternity Benefit
- Every eligible women employee working at OIL will get benefit of this as per the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 & Maternity Benefits (Amendment) Act 2017 & as per the latest government guidelines.
- Women employee will be entitled to Maternity Leave subject to actual work for eighty days in the twelve months preceding the date of her expected delivery.
- Eligible women employee will be applicable for 26 weeks maternity leave. This leave can be split as; 8 weeks before expected delivery date & balance 18 weeks post childbirth.
- For eligible women, expecting after having 2 children, the duration of paid maternity leave shall be 12 weeks (i.e., 6 weeks pre and 6 weeks post expected date of delivery).
- For eligible women, adopting child will be entitled for 12 weeks of maternity leave, from the date of adoption.
- It is an enabling provision relating to "work from home" for women, which may be exercised after the expiry of the 26 weeks' leave period. Depending upon the nature of work, women employees may be able to avail this benefit on terms that are mutually agreed with the employer.
## NSURANCE BENEFITS
## Group Mediclaim Coverage
- All OIL on roll employee & his family (spouse & 2 child upto age of 21) will be covered under GMC.
- Each employee family will get coverage of Rs. 3.00 Lacs per annum under the family floater category (can be used for one or by all family members subject to coverage limit).
- To help employee in critical situation, Management at its own discretion will decide on allocating fund from Buffer Coverage. Decision taken by the management shall be final.
- As per the policy clause, 24 hours hospitalization & 10% co-payment is mandatory to claim under this policy.
- Employee need to adhere the policy governed strictly by the terms and condition of the Mediclaim Policy.
- Employee can opt for Cashless hospitalization option wherever it is available or else can opt for reimbursement option.
- The policy also covers reimbursement of expenses on maternity for the first two confinements as per limits defined in policy.
- Employees opting for cashless provision may produce their identity documents to the hospital before hospitalization and the expenses incurred by them shall be claimed by the hospital with the Third Party Administrator (TPA) to the extent of their eligibility.
- As per standard GMC policy may have some exception, exclusion.
- Employee can refer GMC policy document available with Human Resource Dept.
- In all disputes, the decision of the management shall be final.
## Group Accident Policy
- OIL has cover all on roll employee under this policy with worldwide coverage if minimum hospitalization is 24 hrs.
- Employee will be eligible for Coverage at the rate of 3 Times of his / her Annual CTC.
- The insurance provides relief for any accidents anywhere.

chapters.title: Prevention Of Sexual Harassment At Work
chapters.text:
## POLICY PREFACE
- OIL considers sexual harassment of women at work place as an offence of a very serious nature. It is our endeavor to keep our workplace safe, transparent and friendly for our people to work in. Understanding the employees and giving them the confidence that the workplace is fair, transparent and safe has been a core philosophy. Organization is also committed to promote a work environment that is conductive to the professional growth of its women employees and encourage equality of opportunity.
- The Company has a zero tolerance policy against any kind of gender discrimination of employees at the work place.
- This policy is prepared in line with Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (“Act”). Any modification in the act will automatically applicable to this policy.
## POLICY OBJECTIVE:
- To provide safe, transparent & friendly work environment that female employee with dignity, respect and afford equitable treatment.
- To provide protection against sexual harassment of women at workplace and for the prevention and redressal of complaints of sexual harassment and for matters connected therewith.
## DOCUMENTS
- Written Complaint
- Evidences
- Investigation Report
- Finding of the ICC
## APPLICABILITY,SCOPE AND ENTITLEMENT:
This policy applies to all categories of women employees of Organization including permanent & Contract employees including managerial staff and workmen, temporaries, trainees and employees.
This policy will apply to all complaints of sexual harassment by an employee against another employee irrespective of whether the sexual harassment is alleged to have taken place within or outside the premises.
All women who visit the premises of the company for any purpose, such as customers , visitors etc. (“Aggrieved Woman”);
## MEANINGS OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT
- Sexual harassment includes any one or more of the following unwelcome acts or behavior (whether directly or by implication) namely.
- Physical contact and advances; or
- A demand or request for sexual favors; or
- Making sexually colored remarks; or
- Showing pornography; or
- Any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature;
- Any conduct that has the purpose or the effect of interfering with the individual’s work Performance or creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment and/or submission to such conduct is either an explicit or implicit term or condition of employment and /or submission or rejection of the conduct is used as a basis for making employment While sexual harassment is not limited to the above mentioned points and it includes;
- Unwelcome sexual advances.
- Making unwanted communication through social networking sites, emails, text messages; for sending any kind of a message that is not favorable to a professional relationship and/or are deemed to be offensive by the recipient of such messages.
- Any verbal conduct like the use of sexually colored remarks, innuendoes, derogatory comments, offers of promotion / employment in exchange for sexual favors, graphICC comments on a fellow women colleague’s physical attributes. Sexual harassment also includes addressing women colleagues by terms such as “babe”, “honey”, “darling” , “sweetheart” etc.
- Any unwelcome / unwanted physical contact of a sexual nature. This includes sexually suggestive or offensive touching, deliberate brushing against another’s body. Cornering, blocking, stalking, staring, pinching, fondling etc of a woman co-worker is also included type of sexual harassment.
- Any kind of unwanted visual conduct/ manner such as staring/ leering or displaying any kind of sexually suggestive indecent explicit posters, photography, graffiti, drawings, gestures, inappropriate obscene text messages, emails, letters notes, internet information etc.
- Emotional & psychological harassment in the form of threats and insinuation that the concerned employee’s employment or salary or promotion or appraisal or any other condition of employment will be adversely affected if she does not submit to the sexual demands.
- Any kind of implied or explicit –
- Promises of preferential treatment in employment.
- Threat of detrimental treatment in employment.
- Threat about present or future employment status, may amount to sexual harassment.
- Interference with or creating an intimidating or offensive or hostile work environment
- Humiliating treatment to affect health or safety of a woman co-worker.
## RESPONSIBILITIES REGARDING SEXUAL HARASSMENT
## Employer’s Responsibilities
- To provide a safe working environment at workplace.
- Treat sexual harassment as misconduct
- Display at the conspicuous place in the workplace the penal consequence of the sexual harassment
- Organize workshops and awareness programmers at regular intervals for sensitizing the Employees with the provisions of the Act.

chapters.title: Complaints
chapters.text:
- Any employee with a harassment concern is not comfortable with the informal resolution options or has exhausted such options, may make a formal complaint to the chairperson of the ICC constituted by the management.
- The complaint shall have to be in writing and can be in the form of a letter, preferably within three months from the date of the last incident. Alternatively, the employee can send the complaint through an e-mail.
- The employee is required to disclose her name, department, division and location where she is working so as to enable the chairperson to contact her and take the matter forward.
- Where the woman is unable to make a complaint because of her physical or mental incapacity or death or otherwise, her legal heir or such other person as may be prescribed may make a complaint on her behalf.
## ENQUIRY PROCEDURE
- All the proceedings conducted by the ICC will be confidential.
- The ICC, upon receiving the complaint from the aggrieved person, shall send a copy of the complaint to the Respondent, within a period of 7 days.
- The Respondent shall file a reply in writing to the complaint within a period not extending 10 working days from the date of receipt of the copy of the complaint from the IC.
- The ICC shall call upon any documents like copies of emails/bills/credit card statements etc. which the ICC deems fit to serve as documentary proof.
- The ICC may before initiating the inquiry can, at the request of the aggrieved person, take steps to resolve the matter between the two parties through conciliation; if there is no monetary settlement as a result of the conciliatory proceedings. In case of a settlement, the ICC shall record it in writing.
- The ICC will proceed with the inquiry where no settlement is arrived at through conciliation.
- Both the parties will have a right to be heard and produce evidence to support their claim.
- During the proceeding before the ICC, the parties shall not be allowed to bring in their Advocate to represent them at any stage of the inquiry proceeding.
- The decision of the ICC will be conveyed to the two parties in writing.
- Total time for the investigation should not exceed 1 month from date on which the ICC received the complaint.
- The ICC shall submit a report with its recommendation to the Chief HR/MD for further appropriate action
- MALICIOUS COMPLAINT: If the complaint is found to be malicious or a false complaint, action will be taken against the complainant in accordance with the Code of Conduct/Disciplinary Action Policy of the Company.
- Where such conduct on the part of the accused amounts to a specific offence under the law, appropriate actions will be initiated in accordance with law by making a complaint with the appropriate authority.
- ICC shall conduct such investigation in a timely manner and shall submit a written report containing the findings and the recommendations to the Chief HR/MD as soon as practically possible and in any case ,not later than 90 days from the date of receipt of the complaint.
- The Chief HR/MD will ensure corrective action on the recommendations of the ICC and keep the complainant informed of the same.
- Corrective Actions may include any of the following:
- Certain reliefs can be made available to the Complainant during the pendency of the inquiry.
- The ICC may recommend to the Company to:
- Transfer the Complainant and/or the Respondent to another work place.
- Grant leave to the aggrieved person for up to a period of 3 months.
- Grant any other relief as the ICC deems fit.
- COMPENSATION: If the ICC deems it appropriate for any sum to be paid as compensation to the Complainant, it can determine the amount keeping in mind the following points:
- The mental trauma, pain, suffering and emotional distress caused to the aggrieved person.
- The loss in career opportunity due to the incident of sexual harassment.
- Medical expenses, if any, incurred by the victim for physical or psychiatric treatment.
- The income of the Respondent shall also be taken into consideration while calculating the quantum and mode of monetary compensation.
APPEAL: Any person, aggrieved from the recommendations of the ICC or the non-implementation of its recommendations may prefer to the appropriate legal authority. The appeal shall be preferred within 90 days of the recommendation.
The following process should be followed for expressing and seeking redressal to a grievance:
- Employees may communicate their grievance in writing to their manager first while at the same time, addressing a copy to the concerned department Head. In case the grievance involves the Manager, then the employee can contact the Manager, while simultaneously copying the concerned.
- The concerned manager must immediately acknowledge receipt of the grievance in writing, informing the employee of the receipt of grievance and inviting the employee for a formal meeting.

## PURPOSE:

## OBJECTIVE:
- Foster Total Employee Involvement
- Promote Teamwork
- Recognize and Motivate employees
- Improve Ownership and Accountability at all level.
## APPLICABILITY:
This policy will be applicable to every employee working directly or indirectly with OIL.
## RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Human Resources Department is responsible for preparation & adherence of this policy.
- All Mangers are responsible to make good use of it to achieve above mentioned Objectives
- Suggestion scheme coordinator is responsible for execution & operational activities of the policy.
- Evolution Committee to evaluate benefit in PQCDSM Pre & Post implementation
## DOCUMENTS:
- Suggestion Form
- Suggestion MIS
## SUGGESTION
Any SUGGESTION that is practical, implementable and will result in saving or improvement of operations Or Customer satisfaction (S-Safety, Q-Quality, D-Delivery, C-Cost Saving, P-Productivity) will be treated as a good suggestion / Kaizen.
## Specific areas not applicable for SUGGESTION Scheme:
- Govt. Rules/ Regulations
- Company Policy
- Personal grievance
## HOW SUGGESTION SCHEME OPERATE
- Any employee working directly or indirectly with OIL can give suggestion by following below procedure
- The suggestion scheme coordinator will collect on a weekly basis the suggestion received from the SUGGESTION BOX located at various location of the plant.
- The suggestion scheme coordinator (SSC) will compile all suggestion in soft copy & get it validated by respective supervisor / Manager / HoD. SSC will forward validated, feasible suggestions to Evaluation committee in the First / second week of the month.
- Evaluation committee will evaluate the suggestion / kaizen in First / Second week of the month.
- Feasible / Suitable Suggestion will be accepted & rewarded with a token of appreciation in the Second / Third week of the month & at workplace as per the company’s Reward & Recognition policy.
- Employee is likely to implement the given suggestion along with the concern area in-charge.
- After implementation, employee will be recognize for owning the responsibility of implementing the suggestion / kaizen in the second / third week of the month as per the company’s Reward & Recognition policy.
- The suggestion scheme coordinator will procure gift / coupons / certificate etc. for felicitate the employee & will maintain MIS of it.
## EVALUATION COMMITTEE FOR IMPLEMENTED SUGGESTIONS:
- Evaluation committee will comprise of following personnel.
- WCM
- Safety Manager
- HR Manager
- Production Manager
- Quality Manager
- SCM Manager
- Maintenance Manager
- Purchase Manager
- Finance Manager
- Role of Evaluation committee is to have
- Evaluate benefit in PQCDSM area after implementation of suggestion.
- Suggest reward & recognition based on the outcome.
## SEPARATION OF AN EMPLOYEE
## PURPOSE:
Define appropriate guidelines & process for Separation of an employee.
## OBJECTIVE:
- Consistent, fair and cordial departure of employee.
- Releasing service entitlements.
## APPLICABILITY :
- This policy will be applicable to every employee working directly or indirectly with OIL.
## RESPONSIBILITIES:
- HR department is responsible for preparation, execution & adherence of the policy.
## DOCUMENTS:
- Resignation approved by Reporting Manager & HoD with mutually agreed relieving date
- No Due Certificate
- Exit Interview
- Exit Letter (relieving / Experience Letter)
- Full & Final Settlement
## TYPES OF EMPLOYEE SEPARATION
- On occurrence of any of the below situations, the appropriate Employee Separation process will be initiated:

chapters.title: Resignation
chapters.text:
- An Employee may terminate his employment by tendering Resignation.
- Employee should tender signed resignation to Reporting Manager / HoD for acceptance. Resignation Letter should have date of resignation, reason for the leaving and the last working day of the Employee, including the Notice Period.
- Reporting Manager / HoD should inform & discuss with HR Head on the resignation.
- HoD may discuss retention possibility with HR Manager. Once the retention terms are agreed with HR, the HoD may discuss it with the Employee and communicate the intent for the Employer to retain him/her.
- If the Employee does not, within 5 working days, receive acceptance on his Resignation from his/her HoD, or any communication regarding intent to retain the Employee, then the Employee may directly approach the HR Manager to submit his Resignation.
- In case employee decide to leave, he has to serve Notice Period. Company reserve right to accept or reject Notice Period buy back / Waver off request.
- Refer Notice Period Clause mentioned below in the policy.
The Employer may decide to terminate an Employee, in the following situations.
All such terminations will be carried out in accordance with the local laws
## Termination due to unsatisfactory performance during the Employee’s probationary period
- If an Employee does not satisfactorily complete the probationary period, his/her employment contract may be terminate by giving 15 days notice, as long as the termination occurs within the stated probationary period.
- Employee & Employer may terminate employment contract during probation period with 15 days’ notice.
- On termination concern, Trainee / Employee processed for Full & Final settlement as per term of contract.
## Termination due to unsatisfactory performance of the Employee
- Whenever an Employee’s performance does not matches the expectation or fails to improve to the satisfaction level even after several intimations, and in line with the targets set by concern HoD; then the Employee may be terminate on the grounds of unsatisfactory performance.
- Employer may terminate employee by giving Notice as per the employment letter or by paying Notice Period. Employer reserve sole rights of this & reserve right to explain termination cause to employee.
- On termination concern, Trainee / Employee processed for Full & Final settlement as per term of contract.
- Termination due to disciplinary actions against the Employee.
- An employee can be terminate immediately if he / she found guilty in Legal enquiry conducted by Authorized Enquiry Officer or by internal disciplinary committee.
- In such cases, Employee shall not be eligible to get Payment linked with Performance & Gratuity.
- In case matter is seen in Labour Officer or in Labour Court, required changes will be made in termination & compensation process, which will be as per concern authority orders
- Termination due to the Employee’s inability to work due to a debilitating medical condition, injury, or disability
## Unfit to Work
- In case during Annual Medical Examination or in any of the Medical Health check-up if an employee found & announce to be Unfit to work then in such case employer has to consider concern employee for termination.
- Employer also has the liberty to conduct fitment test of employee in case of any doubt.
- In such termination employee is compensated by Employee State Insurance Corporation as per ESIC Act or by GPA policy or any means states in laws, however Employer also compensate to express courtesy towards its employee.
- On termination concern Trainee / Employee processed for Full & Final settlement as per term of contract.
- In case matter is seen in Labour Officer or in Labour Court, required changes will be made in termination & compensation process which will be as per concern authority orders
- The ultimate aim of this is to avoid & safeguard employee from accident & unwanted injuries.
## Debilitation due to Work Injury or Disability
- If an Employee is a victim of work or any other injury or has a permanent disability, which incapacitates his /her ability to perform as, required at his/her role, it may be decide by the Employer to terminate the employment contract. The ultimate aim of this is to avoid & safeguard employee from accident & unwanted injuries.
- Employer must ensure that permanent disability is asses by ESIC or competent Medical officer & has issued certificate of the same.
- Such Termination intimation shall be to be given Government Officer such as Labour Officer, Factory Inspector, ESIC Officer & Welfare Board.
- In such termination, Employee State Insurance Corporation as per ESIC Act Or GPA as per the policy terms compensates employee, however Employer also compensate to express courtesy towards its employee.
- In case matter is seen in Labour Officer or in Labour Court, required changes will be made in termination & compensation process, which will be as per concern authority orders.

chapters.title: Retirement
chapters.text:
- As per current applicable Laws, retirement of employee shall be on completion of 58 yrs. of age starting from date of birth which employee has declared & evinced at the time of Joining.
- Retiring employee shall ensure smoothening of handing over of his activities to the successor or the person notified by Company.
## Redundancy
- If there is a situation when a role is no longer required for reasons justified by Business requirements, the role may be made Redundant. The reason for Redundancy has no bearing on the individual Employee within the role, and it solely the removal of a role because it is no longer viable in the current Business circumstances. Based on Business decisions, the Employer may decide to make changes to its Organizational Design, resulting in several Redundancies across a location, region or the Group.
- All Redundancy situations will be treated with sensitivity, providing the Employee as much notice as reasonably possible and the Separation processes will be carried out in line with the terms of local legislation.
- Where required, the Employer will notify the local legal and governing bodies regards the Redundancy in advance of any related internal communication.
- Employer may terminate an employee on the grounds of surplus labour or incapacity of employees due to some poor economic grounds.
## End of Employment Contract
- This term refers to a Trainee / Employee / Retainer / Consultant who has signed a Fixed Term Contract with Employer in which contract Start & End date is clearly mentioned.
- Contract will expired on End date until it is extended by both the parties else this contract will be considered as invalid & none of the party liable to each other.
- It is joint responsibility HR Department & relevant HoD to track and manage all definite term employment contracts within their remit, to ensure that appropriate action is taken.
- On termination of contract concern, Trainee / Employee / Retainer / Consultant processed for Full & Final settlement as per term of contract.
